To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the filamentous fungus, A. fumigatus efficiently hydroxylates progesterone to 11 alpha-15 beta-dihydroyprogesterone.
progesterone is transformed by A. fumigatus to 7β-, 11α-, and 15β-hydroxyprogsterone and that these transformations are catalysed by two non-inducibe cytochrome P-450 monooxygenases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a biotechnological process for the production of 15 beta- hydroxyprogesterone, a potent anti-inflammatory compound, by the fungus A. fumigatus.
the isolation and characterization of the microsomal cytochromes P450 from the fungus, Aspergiilus fumigatus which is capable of hydroxylating progesterone at C-7, C-11, and C-15.
the identification of microbial metabolites of steroids and with the elucidation of the enzymatic mechanisms of their formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
A. fumigatus is an efficient steroid 7 beta-, 11 alpha-15 beta-monohydroxylase, but not an efficient steroid 15 beta-dioxygenase.

A. fumigatus is capable of hydroxylating progesterone at 3 sites (7 beta, 11 alpha and 15 beta), that microsomes prepared by Ca2+-precipitation are capable of catalysing the same reactions, that NADPH is required for the hydroxylation reaction and that the cytochrome P448-type azole fungicide ketoconazole inhibits the hydroxylation of progsterone by the microsomes.
A. fumigatus possesses two non-inducable progesterone hydroxylation systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the filamentous fungi, Aspergillu s fumigatus and Aspergillus ochraceus, have a cytochrome P-450 dependent progesterone hydroxylation system that is very similar in its properties to that of mammalian liver.
progesterone is a substrate for the cytochrome P-450 system of A. fumigatus and is hydroxylated by two non-inducibe enzymes.
the filamentous fungi, A. terreus, A. fumigatus and A. nidulans, have a common cytochrome P-450 progesterone 15 beta-hydoxylase, but differ in their cytochrome P 450 progesterone monohydroylases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the ketoconazole is an effective way to prevent the growth and proliferation of the fungi, which can be very helpful in the treatment of fungal diseases.
the 15β-hydroxylase is a non-inducible P450 enzyme.
the use of microsomes can be used in place of whole-cell assays to identify and characterize the specific enzymes involved in a given reaction.
